subject: Synthesizing infra capacity and GPU unit-economics for QBR readout
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Synthesizing infra capacity and GPU unit-economics for QBR readout

Team —

As we pull the QBR package together for the exec readout (week of Apr 26), I want a single synthesis slide + an appendix with the underlying numbers that answers: 

- What is our current committed GPU spend (monthly runrate) vs true-utilized token throughput?
- How much runway do we get from batching and prefix/KV caching improvements (conservative / likely / aggressive)?
- Where are the top three operational risks that could materially increase unit cost next quarter (supply, telemetry gaps, model regressions)?

Deliverables I need by EOD Apr 20: 
- A 1-page slide (bullet + 2 charts) summarizing the 3 points above.
- A linked workbook with the assumptions and sensitivity cells (sheets: commit_vs_utilization, batching_delta, caching_delta).
- Top-3 asks with owners (what we need from infra/product/legal to make changes before the next billing cycle).

I've attached a working workbook (qbr_capacity_model_v2.xlsx) — please update the appropriate tabs, add a short change log, and include provenance for any numbers you alter. Call out any blind spots (metrics we can't produce reliably today).

Priority guidance: emphasize what reduces per-token unit cost while keeping our 99th percentile latency SLO intact. Note tradeoffs between Dedicated reserved slots (predictable throughput) and Hosted with aggressive burst autoscale (lower committed cost but higher variance).

I'll collate inputs and draft slides on Apr 20 afternoon for a quick leadership review.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Director, Infrastructure Economics
Redwood Inference

Attachment: qbr_capacity_model_v2.xlsx (workbook, 1.2MB stub)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Synthesizing infra capacity and GPU unit-economics for QBR readout

Sounds good — I updated the commit_vs_utilization tab with the April telemetry (slot-level utilization, prefetch hit rates). Short notes:

- Current committed spend: $1.85M/mo (cross-account reserved + Dedicated pools).
- Effective utilization (weighted by model seq length & batching mix): 64% (April median); tail remains noisy for short-seq features.
- Batching delta: conservative ~7% cost reduction, likely ~12%, aggressive ~18% (depends on model mix).

I attached a quick PNG of the slot utilization heatmap (slot_utilization_dashboard.png). Two asks for clarity: 
1) Do we include quantization rollout benefits in the base-case or present as an upside scenario?
2) I flagged two pools (eu-west-1-dedicated-3, us-central-burst) with persistent GC stalls — suggests infra ops need a patch before we can count their capacity as reliable.

-Markus
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Attachment: slot_utilization_dashboard.png (image, 480x300 stub)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, markus.klein@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Synthesizing infra capacity and GPU unit-economics for QBR readout

Thanks — good progress. A few leadership notes for the slide:

- Frame the headline as runway impact: "X months of runway at current burn; Y months with batching & caching plan." Leadership wants the concrete trade — avoid deep infra detail on the slide; keep that for the appendix.
- Highlight any asks that require budget shifts or SLA exceptions. I expect one slide with top-3 asks and owners.
- Include the scenario where Dedicated commitments increase by 15% to avoid short-term tail impacts, and the incremental cost vs expected utilization gain.

Also call out any blockers that need a Go/No-Go for the May billing cycle (e.g., KB patch, quant rollout gating).

Please surface 1-2 risks with potential dollar impact ranges. I can sign off on the final slide at 4pm PT Apr 20.

-Lauren
VP, Infrastructure & Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Andrew Park <andrew.park@cloudcore.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Synthesizing infra capacity and GPU unit-economics for QBR readout

Hi Jasmine / Monica —

Quick external note from CloudCore (since we're in the deal loop): our procurement team needs to see expected slot utilization and committed vs burst cost delta for a 12-month term to finalize pricing. Happy to accept the collation in the shared workbook (sheet: cloudcore_procurement_view). We only need a summarized table (monthly committed cost, expected burst delta, expected tokens/sec).

If possible, can you drop that extract by Apr 20 EOD? Procurement will use it for an internal approval on Apr 22.

Thanks —
Andrew Park

CloudCore Inc

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: Andrew Park <andrew.park@cloudcore.com>, procurement@cloudcore.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Synthesizing infra capacity and GPU unit-economics for QBR readout — final collated package

Team — final collated package attached and linked. Summary of what I added:

- Executive slide (one page) with headline runway numbers: runway at current burn = 3.4 months; with conservative batching/caching plan = 4.3 months; aggressive = 5.1 months.
- Appendix workbook updated with CloudCore procurement extract (sheet: cloudcore_procurement_view) and sensitivity bands.
- Top-3 asks with owners: 
  1) Infra Ops: urgent KB patch for GC stalls (owner: Markus) — risk range $60k–$140k QoQ if unaddressed.
  2) Product: priority canary expansion for short-seq routing to improve tail utilization (owner: Vivek) — estimated +4–7% utilization.
  3) Finance: approval for 15% Dedicated top-up for May to stabilize tail (owner: Lauren) — incremental committed cost $275k/mo.

Links & attachments: final slide deck (attached), workbook link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcD_example_qbr_synthesis, HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567/DEAL-890

Next steps: Lauren to review and sign off by 4:00pm PT today. Markus/Vivek/Monica — please confirm the numbers in the workbook are final by 3:00pm PT. Andrew — procurement extract is in the workbook; flag any formatting needs and we will iterate quickly.

Thanks all —
Jasmine Liu
Director, Infrastructure Economics
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sprint_ask_rundown.pdf (PDF, 480KB); qbr_capacity_model_v2.xlsx (updated)
